title: The worker role's gate add command names a --do per option, so a worker never hand-edits an item file for a missing do map
goal: The worker role file (agents/worker.md) gives the provisional gate command with a --do OPTION=ID for each option, so a worker's gate has its do map from the start, backlog.py check warns of no missing do on it and no worker hand-edits an item file to add one (gate add takes --do only at creation and gate remove is operator-only: seen at SP-avwlotax and SP-sqgyoiaz)

run: import sys;ls=[l for l in open('agents/worker.md',encoding='utf-8') if 'gate add ID --kind provisional' in l];print(ls);sys.exit(0 if ls and all('--do' in l for l in ls) else 1)

gates.question: What does the role file give each --do OPTION=ID of a worker's gate as its ID?
options: the worker's own item id: the work it is doing carries the chosen option out
the id of a follow-up item the worker files for each option

notes: Merged from ST-2vhaoflk “A worker's gate that the class rule makes blocking can get its do entries after it is added” at the 2026-10-13 draft triage: Premise holds (gate has only add/remove/host-unchecked, no `do` verb; bl_check.py:1049 warns; seen SP-avwlotax and SP-sqgyoiaz), but passing --do per option up front, which ST-xgaj3rlb states, removes the recurrence; the added-later `gate do` verb is optional Its goal: Retrospective of SP-avwlotax: ST-jv27pfin's worker added g2 as provisional; gate add printed 'made blocking' (class agents-rule) and backlog.py check then warned that g2 has no do for either option, which the worker could not repair: gate add takes --do only at creation and gate remove is operator-only. A gate's do entries can be added to an existing gate by its item's worker (or gate add's made-blocking message tells it to pass --do up front), so check has no such warning after a worker's gate. Its checks: {"run": ["python3", "_tools/backlog.py", "gate", "do", "--help"]} Its touches: _tools/bl_items.py, _tools/backlog.py, kb/_self/backlog.md, kb/_self/tools.md, kb/_self/code.md Planned at the 2026-10-13 draft triage (sprint 14 of 15, "Gates and filing: words do not misclass a gate, workers file no duplicates and add gates with their do map"): it fixes a failure that recurred in recent sprints and blocks the EP-gzr4mmkm fitness test that a content sprint lands on headless Sonnet workers with no operator step beyond its gates.
